exposure: previous infection with the same organism during the previous 12 months
urinary catheter in the past 30 days
cardiac catheterization in the past 30 days
cohort: Non-immunocompromised pediatric patients (18 years of age or younger) hospitalized at the American University of Beirut Medical Center with infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria between 2009 and 2017.
finding: A high prevalence of infections with multidrug resistant Gram-negative bacteria (47.8%) was observed in non-immunocompromised pediatric patients in Lebanon, with particularly alarming MDR rates among Escherichia coli (64.3%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (59.1%), and Acinetobacter species (70.6%).
